text:
Predicates:
GRE(x) ::: x is the GRE test.
Cost(x, y) ::: x costs y dollars.
Cheaper(x, y) ::: x is cheaper than y.
Provides(x, y, z) ::: x provides y to z.
FinancialAid(x) ::: x is financial aid.
Applicant(x, y) ::: x is an applicant for y.
Prove(x, y) ::: x proves y.
EconomicHardship(x) ::: x is economic hardship.
Lives(x, y) ::: x lives in y.
SingleParentFamily(y) ::: y is a single-parent family.
FewResources(x) ::: x has few resources available to them.
Applying(x, y) ::: x is applying to take y.
Tom ::: Tom.
Premises:
Cost(gre, 205) ∧ Cheaper(gre, 300) ::: It costs $205 to take the GRE test, which is cheaper than $300.
Provides(ets, financialAid, ∀x (GRE(y) ∧ Applicant(x, y) ∧ Prove(x, EconomicHardship(x)))) ::: ETS provides financial aid to those GRE applicants who prove economic hardship.
(Lives(x, SingleParentFamily(y)) ∨ FewResources(x)) → Prove(x, EconomicHardship(x)) ::: Those living in single-parent families or having few resources available to them can prove economic hardship.
Lives(tom, SingleParentFamily(y)) ∧ FewResources(tom) ::: Tom lives in a single-parent family. Tom's dad has been out of work, and Tom has few resources available to him.
Applying(tom, gre) ::: Tom is applying to take the GRE test.
Conclusion:
Cheaper(gre, 300) ::: It costs below US $300 to take the GRE test.
